QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_18

question.text: The exchange-level open interest in GOI bond futures on a short-maturity bucket underlying is Rs. 10,000 crores, with a Rs. 200 crore bucket floor. A client currently holds bond futures worth Rs. 280 crores. How much additional position can the client take?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per pages 234-236 of the NISM Series IV workbook, the client-level position limit for GOI bond futures is 3% of exchange open interest or the maturity-bucket floor, whichever is higher. 3% of Rs. 10,000 crore = Rs. 300 crore; comparing with the Rs. 200 crore floor, the higher is Rs. 300 crore. Remaining capacity = 300 - 280 = Rs. 20 crore. The Trap: Rs. 220 crore would arise from using the lower-of rule the workbook does not use. Rs. 500 crore ignores the client's existing position. Rs. 300 crore is the limit itself, not the remaining capacity after subtracting the current position. Note: Per page 235, exchange-level overall IRD open positions on a specific underlying must not exceed 25% of the outstanding underlying bond; this exchange cap is separate from the open-interest-linked client limit applied above.
